newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia emphasises government's role in telecoms.
newsitem.headline: Asia emphasises government's role in telecoms.

text.p: Governments have vital roles to play to support the telecommunications industry in Asia during this period of liberalisation, a panel of industry leaders and government officials said on Monday.
The officials were speaking at the Asia Telecom Forum, part of the Asia Telecom 97 trade fair here.
"Where infrastructure is concerned, the government must take the lead because governments take the long term view." said John Chen, Singapore Minister of State for Communications.
Government should also provide part of the funds where its investment would help to convince the private sector of commercial viability, he said.
Yang Xianzu, China Vice Minister of Post and Telecommunications, said China remained committed to heavy investment in telecommunications.

China expects to spend US$12 billion a year in telecommunications in the near future, 80 percent of which would come from government funds, he said. He added that China collected some US$5 billion a year in call-charge revenue.

Joop Ave, Indonesia Minister of Tourism, Post and Telecommunications, said governments had to acknowledge most telecoms research and development was being done in the West, and Asia should set aside funds to train its people there.

Chen said besides making sure everyone had access to information technology facilities, governments had to provide a more liberal environment for ideas to flourish, especially in the provision of contents.
Several panelists thought Asia could lead in providing contents that were tailored for Asian needs if the right environment was created.
Others raised the difficulty of regulating an industry where technology changes rapidly but reiterated regulation still had to be done.
Most panelists agreed co-operation between countries and partnerships with Western telecom companies were vital to lift Asia to an equal footing with Western economies.

Serge Tchuruk, chairman and chief executive officer of France-based Alcatel Alsthom, said: "The government should not stop promoting telecommunications even in a privatised environment...Don't forget to develop technology that is born here, don't disregard content."
